messages:
michael: throwing an idea out: hybrid handoff for admission->coalescer. combine cheap copy for SLA traffic and pointer-reserve for best-effort to get both safety and perf.
anya: curious how you plan to implement the reserve. pointer-reserve needs deterministic ownership so we don't free buffers mid-run.
michael: epoch-based reservation. admission tags buffer with epoch N when handed off; coalescer advances a commit marker when done. GC reclaims epochs < committed_min_epoch.
sam: bench note: pointer-reserve lowered p50 by ~3ms on staging but we saw intermittent p99 spikes tied to collector pauses. does epoch smoothing help?
michael: smoothing + small prefetch copies for hot paths. if a buffer is 'hot' or long-lived we proactively copy to a pinned region to avoid GC interference.
anya: observability: emit `batch.handoff.kind` and `batch.handoff.epoch` as low-cardinality fields. also emit `batch.handoff.copy_reason` when we proactively copy.
infra-bot: plan: feature-flag "hybrid-handoff" -> canary -> observe p50/p95/p99 per SLA bucket.
sam: agree on per-tenant opt-in and gating by SLA p99. also add a chaos test that injects GC pauses to validate tail safety.
michael: action: i'll prototype epoch allocator + copy-fallback, add small telemetry, and open RFC addendum.
anya: please include simulation that tests starvation and priority inversion.
michael: will do. thanks all.
